one_liner: Dependency-free C++17 WebAssembly 1.0 interpreter whose eager parse-and-instantiate beats Cranelift JIT runtimes and WAMR fast-interp on startup.
what_it_does: Fizzy is a pedantic, deterministic WebAssembly 1.0 (MVP) interpreter from Ipsilon, aimed at blockchain-style embedding: binary format only, no text format, no proposals. It is a static library with a public C API (fizzy_parse, fizzy_instantiate / fizzy_resolve_instantiate with host-function imports, fizzy_execute), an internal C++ API, a CMake package (fizzy::fizzy) and a Rust crate; optional runtime metering (ticks) and a call-depth bound are exposed through an ExecutionContext. It is not a drop-in for the Wasmtime/Wasmer/wasm-c-api embedding APIs.
how_it_is_fast: Parsing and validation run in one pass (the spec's validation algorithm with a control-frame stack) that emits a compact internal code: opcodes and their immediates in one byte array, with branch targets and stack-drop counts resolved at parse time so execution keeps no control stack. Each function's maximum operand-stack height is precomputed, so arguments, locals and operand stack share one allocation (128-byte inline buffer, heap above that). There is no code generation, so startup is a linear parse, which is why its startup geomean is 83-92x lower than Wasmer and Wasmtime with Cranelift JIT compilation (derived from page data); execution is a plain switch-dispatch loop, with metering compiled in or out by a template parameter.
when_to_use: Short-lived modules where parse + validate + instantiate dominates and you would otherwise pay JIT compile time (Wasmtime/Wasmer Cranelift startup geomean ~1500-1600x the fastest runtime vs Fizzy 17.8x on EPYC 7763).
Deterministic contract execution that needs per-instruction gas metering, a call-depth bound and a hard memory cap from a small, heavily tested C++17 codebase.
Embedding a WebAssembly 1.0 engine into a C or C++ host with no third-party dependencies, via a C API or CMake find_package.
Modules that use only WebAssembly 1.0 features and small-to-medium code sections (it won bz2, coremark, argon2 and erc20 startup against V8 on EPYC).
when_not_to_use: Compute-heavy or long-running guest code: execution geomean is 45.6x the fastest runtime vs WAMR fast-interp 17.1x and V8 1.05x on EPYC 7763, and Fizzy's own v0.5.0 table shows wasm3 0.4.7 at 26% of Fizzy's execution time.

Modules that need post-MVP features (bulk memory, SIMD, multi-value, reference types, tail calls); the wasmi-benchmarks harness skips Fizzy on its bulk-ops, fibonacci-tail and counter-param execute tests.

Running WASI programs: fizzy-wasi implements only a limited subset of wasi_snapshot_preview1 over uvwasi, failed the libsodium suite (no poll_oneoff), and has open memory-corruption reports (#857 invalid write in fd_write, #858 invalid read) unanswered since 2024-08.

Very large modules or when startup is the only metric: lazy validators start faster (Wasmi v2 lazy x1.37, Wasm3 lazy x2.77) and V8 beat Fizzy on ffmpeg (35 ms vs 215 ms) and spidermonkey (11 ms vs 52 ms).
Projects that need an actively maintained engine: no code changes since 2023-03-03, and big-endian targets are rejected at CMake configure time.

integration.dependencies: none for the library (uvwasi only for the optional fizzy-wasi tool; test tools pull dependencies through Hunter)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake 3.15; GCC 15/libstdc++ 15 and libc++ 19+ (Xcode 16) need small source shims (missing <algorithm> include, std::char_traits<unsigned char>)
integration.platforms: little-endian only; x86-64 and 32-bit x86 (SSE2 required for compliant floats); aarch64 macOS ran in wasmi-benchmarks via the fizzyx bindings, but upstream issue #709 'Support Apple Silicon natively' is still open
integration.thread_safety: not documented; ExecutionContext is described as per execution thread and an Instance owns its mutable memory and globals, so do not share an Instance across threads without external locking
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same job as Wasmtime/Wasmer/WAMR (load, link host functions, call exports) but its own C API, at most one result per function and only function imports in the fizzyx Rust bindings; no wasm-c-api support (issue #696 open)

gotchas: Each WebAssembly call recurses into execute() on the native C++ stack, up to CallStackLimit = 2048 nested calls before trapping; size host thread stacks for that depth.

Fizzy does not touch the floating-point environment: the host must keep round-to-nearest and must not enable FP exception traps (feenableexcept), or results become non-compliant or unpredictable; x87 builds need -msse2 -mfpmath=sse.

fizzy_instantiate caps linear memory at 256 MB (4096 pages) by default unless memory_pages_limit is raised (max 65536 pages = 4 GB); memory is a zero-filled std::basic_string<uint8_t> allocated at instantiate.

Upstream no longer builds unmodified on GCC 15 (capi.cpp uses std::transform without <algorithm>) or libc++ 19+ (no char_traits<unsigned char>); the fizzyx crate force-includes a compat_shim.hpp, and you would need the same patch.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Fizzy over wasm3, WAMR or Wasmi when you want a dependency-free C++17 interpreter with gas metering, strict spec conformance and fast eager startup, and execution speed is secondary; wasm3 and WAMR fast-interp run code roughly 2.7-4x faster, Wasmi (lazy) and DLR-FT wasm-interpreter start faster, and toywasm or submilli-wasm give similar startup with more proposal support.
verified_claims_summary: In Robin Freyler's wasmi-benchmarks startup suite (criterion timing of parse + validate + instantiate of 7 modules through his fizzyx Rust bindings; Fizzy built by cmake-rs, which resolves the Cargo bench profile to CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, i.e. -O3 -DNDEBUG without LTO, C++ compiler version not stated), Fizzy's geomean on an AMD EPYC 7763 was 17.83x the per-case fastest runtime versus WAMR fast-interp 56.73x, V8 33.27x, Wasmer Cranelift 1484x and Wasmtime Cranelift 1634x. The harness unwraps Module::new, so each reported time is a successful parse, not an early error; the win is startup only, and execution on the same suite is about 2.7x slower than WAMR fast-interp.
status_note: Dormant: the last code change was 2023-03-03 (last release 0.8.0, 2022-06-28, also the latest fizzy crate), later commits are README-only and 2024 security reports are unanswered; Apache-2.0, dependency-free and small enough to vendor if you carry the GCC 15/libc++ 19 build patches.
